financeRollup: Thursday’s U.S. close reversed the prior rebound, with the S&P 500 down 0.9% and Brent up 2.4%; Friday’s Asian session was mixed as Kospi and Hang Seng rose but Nikkei slipped. cards.summary: AP reported that Tehran rejected Trump’s latest economic threats on Thursday while the wider Iran war continued to keep shipping, energy and humanitarian access unsettled.
detail: Associated Press reported on Aug. 20 that Iran dismissed President Donald Trump’s economic threats and warned of public resentment as the conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption continued. cards.summary: El País reported a lightning-caused fire near Segorbe and Gátova after intense storms; AEMET-linked reports recorded thousands of strikes, dry storm conditions and damaging wind in the province.
detail: El País reported on Aug. 21 that the electrical storms crossing the Valencian Community had produced more than 4,000 lightning strikes and ignited several fires. The Generalitat’s main concern was a fire between Segorbe and Gátova in the Sierra de la Calderona; AEMET said only 0.2 litres per square metre fell at Segorbe and identified a nearby positive-polarity strike at 20:06 with intensity above 37.6 kiloamperes.

The shift matters because the region moved from extreme heat into a compound risk: dry ground, wind, lightning and sudden rainfall can create both fire spread and flash-flood exposure. Separate reporting recorded downbursts near 150 km/h and heavy rain in parts of Valencia.

The immediate watch is the fire perimeter, road and outdoor-access restrictions, and the next AEMET warning update. The local impact remains time-sensitive; this card does not assume that every reported fire or closure is fully resolved.

cards.summary: Civil Protection said heavy rain and storms would affect northern and eastern Spain and the Balearics; El País reported the broader pattern could bring strong storms and hail through Monday.

The next useful check is the province-level AEMET map and Civil Protection update, especially where dry ground, lightning and strong wind overlap. Forecast totals and warning levels remain subject to revision.

cards.title: U.S. stocks fall as bond-market relief fades
cards.summary: AP reported the S&P 500 fell 0.9%, the Dow 1.3% and Nasdaq 1% on Thursday as oil, inflation and debt worries outweighed Treasury’s buyback support.
detail: Associated Press reported that the S&P 500 fell 0.9% to 7,641.16 on Thursday, Aug. 20; the Dow dropped 703.84 points, or 1.3%, to 52,759.21; and the Nasdaq fell 1% to 26,067.17. It was the market’s worst day in three weeks.

AP linked the move to renewed bond-market pressure, higher oil prices and concern about U.S. government debt. Brent crude rose 2.4% to $93.78, while the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.70% after a brief response to the buyback announcement.
This is a completed-session description, not a forecast. The next uncertainty is whether Treasury’s larger buybacks can change the yield path when debt supply and inflation concerns remain.

cards.title: Fed minutes revive the possibility of higher rates
cards.summary: Minutes from the July meeting say many officials would likely support higher rates if inflation fails to decline, even as the September decision remains uncertain.
detail: The Federal Reserve released minutes from its July 28–29 meeting on Aug. 19. AP reported that many officials thought the central bank might need to lift its short-term rate in coming months if inflation did not subside; the committee had voted 9–3 to keep the rate near 3.6%.

The minutes identified inflation risks from the Iran war, tariffs and heavy AI-infrastructure investment. AP also reported that investors still expected the Fed to hold in September, while noting that market expectations could change.
The next evidence is incoming inflation, energy and labor data rather than a predetermined policy move. This card describes the policy signal and carries no investment recommendation.
